questions.prompt: Do you like looking at photographs of yourself?
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like to look at photos of me. It is fun. I like to see my friends and family too. But sometimes I don't like my face.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's okay to look at photos of myself. Sometimes it's nice to see how I looked in the past. For example, I have some photos from my vacation last year, and they remind me of good times. However, I don't like all the photos. Some of them are not very good!
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm a bit fifty-fifty about it. On one hand, it's lovely to look back on old photos and relive good memories. But the thing is, I tend to be my own worst critic, so I often end up nitpicking little details. I suppose as long as I don't take it too seriously, it's fine.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men rasmlarni yaxshi ko'raman. Men xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, o'zimning rasmlariga qarashni yoqtiraman. Bu qiziqarli. Do'stlarim va oilamni ham ko'rishni yoqtiraman. Lekin ba'zida yuzim yoqmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
O'zimning rasmlarimga qarash yaxshi deb o'ylayman. Ba'zida o'tmishda qanday ko'ringanimni ko'rish yoqimli.
Masalan, o'tgan yili ta'tilimdan olingan rasmlarim bor va ular menga yaxshi vaqtlarni eslatadi.
Lekin, menga hamma rasmlar ham yoqmaydi. Ularning ba'zilari unchalik yaxshi emas!
questions.uzSampleB2: O'zimning suratlarimga qarash haqida aralash tuyg'ularga egaman. Bir tomondan, o'tmishdagi tajribalarni eslash va vaqt o'tishi bilan qanday o'zgarganimni ko'rish juda yoqimli bo'lishi mumkin. Eski suratlarga qarash ko'pincha yoqimli xotiralarni esga soladi va hayotimning turli bosqichlari bilan qayta bog'lanishga yordam beradi. Biroq, boshqa tomondan, ba'zida suratlarda o'z tashqi ko'rinishimni haddan tashqari tanqid qilaman. Ko'rinadigan kamchiliklarga e'tibor qaratish yoki o'zimni boshqalar bilan solishtirish oson, bu har doim ham ijobiy tajriba emas. Shunday qilib, shaxsiy fotosuratlarning nostalgik qadrini qadrlasam ham, ularga o'zimni sog'lom qabul qilish bilan yondashishga harakat qilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you like looking at photographs of yourself?...
idioms: freeze a moment in time - "vaqtni muzlatib qo'yish"
"A picture is worth a thousand words" - "Bir surat mingta so'zga teng"
in the blink of an eye - "ko'z ochib yumguncha"
sentenceStarters: "Honestly speaking, I find looking at photographs of myself to be a reflective experience." - "Rostini aytsam, o'zimning suratlarimga qarashni tahliliy tajriba deb bilaman."

"From my perspective, photographs serve as timeless memories that capture the essence of who I am." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, suratlar mening kimligimni aks ettiruvchi abadiy xotiralar sifatida xizmat qiladi."

"I'd have to say that photographs of myself offer a fascinating glimpse into different phases of my life." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, mening suratlarim hayotimning turli davrlariga qiziqarli nazar tashlash imkonini beradi."

questions.sampleAnswer: To be perfectly honest, I really enjoy looking at photographs of myself, but not out of vanity. For me, these photographs serve as a social experience, capturing moments and memories that I cherish deeply. It's incredibly fascinating to reflect on personal growth and change over the years. As the saying goes, "a picture is worth a thousand words", and I often look back at my photos to pick up on things I might have missed at the moment. They remind me of the people I've met, the places I've been, and the experiences I've had. In this fast-paced world, it's a walk down memory lane that allows me to let my hair down and appreciate the journey of life. Overall, while some may find it slightly self-indulgent, I believe that photographs of oneself can be a powerful tool for self-reflection and nostalgia.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Rostini aytsam, o'zimning suratlarimga qarash menga juda yoqadi, lekin bu manmanlikdan emas. Men uchun bu suratlar ijtimoiy tajriba vazifasini o'taydi, men qadrlaydigan lahzalar va xotiralarni aks ettiradi. Yillar davomida shaxsiy o'sish va o'zgarishlar haqida o'ylash juda qiziq. Aytishlaricha, "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi", va men ko'pincha o'sha paytda e'tibordan chetda qoldirgan narsalarni aniqlash uchun o'z suratlarimga qaytib qarayman. Ular menga uchratgan odamlarimni, borgan joylarimni va boshdan kechirgan tajribalarimni eslatadi. Bu tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda, bu xotiralar bo'ylab sayohat bo'lib, hayot yo'lini qadrlashga imkon beradi. Umuman olganda, ba'zilar buni biroz o'ziga bino qo'yish deb hisoblashlari mumkin bo'lsa-da, menimcha, o'zining suratlari o'z-o'zini tahlil qilish va nostalji uchun kuchli vosita bo'lishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Do you have any animals in your home as a pet?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I have a cat. His name is Mimi. Mimi is black. I like Mimi.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I have a pet. It's a fish. It's small and orange. I like to watch it swim. I clean its bowl every week because it gets dirty.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I do have a pet. I have a rabbit. Her name is Daisy. I think she's very cute and fluffy. I like to give her carrots and lettuce. However, she can be a bit messy sometimes, but I still love her.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, actually I've got a cat called Milo, and honestly he's the heart of our home. I got him from a shelter a couple of years ago, and he's really come out of his shell since then. He can be a bit of a handful when he knocks things over, but he keeps me company and cheers me up after a long day.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Mening mushugim bor. Uning ismi Mimi. Mimi qora. Menga Mimi yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menda uy hayvonim bor. Bu baliq. U kichkina va to'q sariq rangda. Unga suzishini tomosha qilish menga yoqadi. Men uning idishini har hafta tozalayman, chunki u iflos bo'lib qoladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menda uy hayvonim bor. Menda bir quyon bor. Uning ismi Daisy. Menimcha, u juda yoqimtoy va yumshoq. Unga sabzi va salat berishni yaxshi ko'raman.
Ammo, u ba'zan biroz tartibsiz bo'lishi mumkin, lekin men uni baribir yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, uyimda itim bor, mahalliy boshpanadan qutqarib olgan beozor teriyer zotli it. Uning ismi Buster. Dastlab olganimda u juda qo'rqoq edi, lekin hozir u ishonchli va o'ynoqi do'st. Uning yonimda bo'lishi meni ko'proq sayr qilish uchun tashqariga chiqishga undaydi va menimcha, bu mening umumiy farovonligimni sezilarli darajada yaxshiladi. Garchi u ancha tuk to'ksa ham, u olib keladigan quvonch noqulaylikdan ancha ustun turadi.

questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I absolutely adore animals, and I grew up with pets around me. Currently, I have a dog named Max, who is a delightful Labrador Retriever. He's not just a pet; he's part of the family. Every morning, he greets me with a wagging tail and an infectious enthusiasm that brightens my day. Having Max has been a profound experience because I've learned to be more responsible and compassionate. There’s "nothing like family" to comfort you, and in this sense, Max provides that unconditional love and companionship that is truly invaluable.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Ha, men hayvonlarni juda yaxshi ko'raman va men atrofimda uy hayvonlari bilan o'sganman. Hozirda menda Maks ismli it bor, u juda yoqimli Labrador Retriever. U shunchaki uy hayvoni emas; u oilaning bir qismi. Har kuni ertalab u meni dumini likillatib va kunimni yoritadigan yuqumli ishtiyoq bilan kutib oladi. Maksning borligi juda katta tajriba bo'ldi, chunki men mas'uliyatliroq va rahmdil bo'lishni o'rgandim. Sizni ovutadigan "oiladan yaxshiroq narsa yo'q" va shu ma'noda Maks chinakam bebaho bo'lgan shartsiz sevgi va hamrohlikni ta'minlaydi.

questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like reading books. They are interesting and I learn new things. Sometimes the stories are sad, but I like them. I read before bed.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like reading books a lot. I think it's a good way to relax and learn new things. For example, I recently read a book about history, and it was very interesting. However, I don't always have time to read as much as I'd like to. I usually read before going to sleep.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I'm a big reader, to be honest. There's nothing better than curling up with a good novel after a hectic day. I mostly go for thrillers because they really keep me on the edge of my seat. I suppose reading also helps me switch off from screens and unwind properly.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men kitoblarni yaxshi ko'raman. Kitoblar yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men kitob o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman. Ular qiziqarli va men yangi narsalarni o'rganaman. Ba'zan hikoyalar qayg'uli bo'ladi, lekin ular menga yoqadi. Men yotishdan oldin o'qiyman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men kitob o'qishni juda yaxshi ko'raman. Menimcha, bu dam olish va yangi narsalarni o'rganishning yaxshi usuli.
Masalan, yaqinda men tarix haqida kitob o'qidim va u juda qiziqarli edi.
Lekin, har doim ham men xohlaganimcha o'qishga vaqtim bo'lmaydi. Men odatda uxlashdan oldin o'qiyman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men kitob o'qishni yoqtiraman. Men buni rag'batlantiruvchi va boyituvchi faoliyat deb bilaman. Bu menga turli dunyolarga qochishga va yangi g'oyalarni o'rganishga imkon beradi. Men kitob o'qish turli madaniyatlar va nuqtai nazarlarni tushunishimni qanday kengaytirishini ayniqsa qadrlayman. Garchi menda har doim xohlaganimcha vaqt bo'lmasa-da, men kitob o'qishni odatiy kun tartibimning bir qismiga aylantirishga harakat qilaman, chunki men buni shaxsiy o'sish uchun qimmatli deb hisoblayman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you like reading books?...
idioms: bookworm - "I've always been a bookworm, finding comfort in the written word since childhood." - "Har doim kitobxon bo‘lganman, bolaligimdan yozma so‘zlarda taskin topaman."
"A room without books is like a body without a soul, and I can't imagine my life devoid of them." - "Kitobsiz xona jonsiz tanaga o'xshaydi, va men ularni hayotimdan tasavvur qila olmayman."
page-turner - "Whenever I discover a page-turner, I become completely engrossed until the very end." - "Har safar qiziqarli kitob topganimda, oxirigacha butunlay sho‘ng‘ib ketaman."
phrases: extensive collection - "I take pride in my extensive collection of literary works that spans various genres and eras." - "Turli janrlar va davrlarni qamrab oluvchi keng kollektsiyamdan faxrlanaman."
avid reader - "Being an avid reader, I find solace and inspiration within the pages of a good book." - "Qizg'in o'quvchi sifatida yaxshi kitob sahifalarida taskin va ilhom topaman."
literary treasures - "My bookshelf is adorned with literary treasures that have shaped my worldview." - "Kitob javonim mening dunyoqarashimni shakllantirgan adabiy xazinalar bilan bezatilgan."
sentenceStarters: "Honestly speaking, I find immense joy in delving into the world of books, as they transport me to realms beyond my imagination." - "Rostini aytsam, kitoblar olamiga sho‘ng‘ishdan ulkan zavq olaman, chunki ular meni tasavvurimdan tashqaridagi olamlarga olib boradi."

"From my perspective, reading is not just a hobby, but a profound journey into diverse cultures and histories." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, o'qish nafaqat bir mashg'ulot, balki turli madaniyatlar va tarixlarga chuqur sayohatdir."

"I'd have to say that literature has always been a cornerstone of my personal development and intellectual growth." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, adabiyot har doim mening shaxsiy rivojlanishim va intellektual o‘sishimning asosiy poydevori bo‘lib kelgan."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely, I genuinely adore reading books. It's a social experience that allows me to dive into different worlds and experience a myriad of perspectives. Reading has been a fundamental part of my life since childhood. I vividly remember the first time I picked up a novel and got lost in its pages; it was as if the characters had jumped off the page and into my imagination.

Honestly, I believe that reading is not just a hobby; it's a gateway to knowledge and personal development. Books have the power to transform one's mindset and broaden one's horizons. As the saying goes, "A reader lives a thousand lives before he dies". This "quote" perfectly encapsulates my experience with reading.

Moreover, in today's fast-paced world, I find reading to be a therapeutic escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. It provides me with a sense of tranquility and allows me to let my hair down, immersing myself in stories that are both profoundly inspiring and incredibly entertaining. Therefore, not only do I like reading books, but I also consider it an indispensable aspect of my existence.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta, men kitob o‘qishni chin dildan yaxshi ko‘raman. Bu menga turli olamlarga sho‘ng‘ib, ko‘plab nuqtai nazarlarni his qilish imkonini beradigan ijtimoiy tajriba. Kitob o‘qish bolaligimdan beri hayotimning muhim qismi bo‘lib kelgan. Birinchi marta roman olib, uning sahifalariga g‘arq bo‘lganimni yorqin eslayman; go‘yo qahramonlar sahifadan sakrab chiqib, xayolimga ko‘chib o‘tgandek bo‘ldi.

Rostini aytsam, menimcha, kitob o‘qish shunchaki xobbi emas; bu bilim va shaxsiy rivojlanishga yo‘l ochuvchi darvoza. Kitoblar odamning fikrlash tarzini o‘zgartirish va ufqlarini kengaytirishga qodir. Maqolda aytilganidek, "Kitobxon o‘lmasdan oldin mingta hayot kechiradi". Bu "ibora" kitob o‘qish bilan bog‘liq tajribamni mukammal tarzda ifodalaydi.

Bundan tashqari, bugungi tez sur’atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda men kitob o‘qishni kundalik hayotning shovqin-suronidan terapevtik qochish deb bilaman. Bu menga xotirjamlik hissini beradi va chuqur ilhomlantiruvchi va nihoyatda qiziqarli bo‘lgan hikoyalarga sho‘ng‘ib, dam olishimga imkon beradi. Shuning uchun, men nafaqat kitob o‘qishni yaxshi ko‘raman, balki uni hayotimning ajralmas qismi deb ham bilaman.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see a man. He is on the street.

I see a bus. People are on the bus.
questions.sampleA2:
In the first picture, I see a man. He is waiting for a car, I think. He has a backpack.

And in the second picture, I see a bus and many people are sitting. One woman is looking at her phone.
questions.sampleB1:
Okay, in the first picture, there's a man standing on the side of the road. He looks like he's trying to get a taxi or something. He has a bag, so maybe he's traveling.

In the second picture, I see a bus full of people. Some are old, some are young. They are all sitting and doing different things. I think it's a normal bus ride.
questions.sampleB2: So in the first picture, there's a young guy standing on a busy city street with his arm up, clearly trying to flag down a taxi. He's wearing an orange body-warmer over a grey jumper and a backpack, so I'd say he's heading somewhere. In the second one, we're inside a packed bus with bright yellow poles. There's a real mix of passengers, from an elderly woman glued to her phone to a couple of young women chatting away. All in all, both shots capture everyday city travel.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men bir erkakni ko'ryapman. U ko'chada.

Men bir avtobusni ko'ryapman. Odamlar avtobusda.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Birinchi rasmda men bir odamni ko'ryapman. U mashina kutyapti, menimcha. Uning ryukzaki bor.

Va ikkinchi rasmda men avtobusni ko'ryapman va ko'p odamlar o'tiribdi. Bir ayol telefoniga qarayapti.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda yo'lning chetida turgan bir odam bor. U taksi to'xtatmoqchi yoki shunga o'xshaydi. Uning sumkasi bor, shuning uchun ehtimol u sayohat qilayotgandir.

Ikkinchi rasmda odamlarga to'la avtobusni ko'ryapman. Ba'zilari keksa, ba'zilari yosh. Ularning hammasi o'tirib, turli xil ishlar bilan band. Menimcha, bu oddiy avtobusda sayohat.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda bir odam avtomobil to'xtatishga harakat qilayotganini ko'rsatadi, yoki hech bo'lmaganda gavjum shahar muhitida mashina to'xtatmoqchi. U oddiy kiyingan va uning yelkasida ryukzaki bor, bu uning sayohatchi yoki talaba bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Uning yorqin rangli jileti kulrang shahar manzarasi bilan kontrast hosil qiladi.

Ikkinchi rasmda avtobusning ichki qismi tasvirlangan, u turli xil yo'lovchilar bilan to'la. Hamma o'z ishlariga berilib ketganday, telefonlaridan foydalanishdan tortib, shunchaki derazadan tashqariga qarashgacha, jim kuzatuv hissi bor. Bu jamoat transportining zerikarli, ammo qiziqarli voqeligini va shahar qatnovining umumiy tajribasini ta'kidlaydi.

"From my perspective, these images capture the essence of life's myriad experiences, each telling its own unique story." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, bu rasmlar hayotning turli xil tajribalarining mohiyatini qamrab oladi, har biri o'ziga xos hikoyani aytib beradi."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first image, I can see a young man who appears to be trying to catch a ride on a busy street. His fashion choice is rather striking, with an orange puffer vest over a grey sweater, which adds a splash of color to the scene. The presence of sunglasses hints at a sunny day, which might explain why he's out and about. The backpack he carries suggests that he's possibly on a journey or just heading somewhere important. The cityscape in the background, with its tall buildings and busy street, paints a picture of urban hustle and bustle, "a city that never sleeps." This image captures the essence of metropolitan life, where everyone seems to be on the move.

As for the second image, it depicts a bus interior filled with passengers of diverse ages, each engaged in their own world. The senior couple at the front catches my eye, particularly the woman who is engrossed in her smartphone, a sight that shows how technology bridges the gap across generations. The vibrant blue and yellow interiors of the bus add a touch of brightness to this otherwise routine scene. Further down, the younger passengers are either chatting away or caught up in their digital worlds, illustrating how public transport becomes a microcosm of society. It’s incredibly fascinating to see how these images, despite being so different, tell a story of human connection and daily life.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi suratda men band ko'chada mashina to'xtatmoqchi bo'lib turgan yosh yigitni ko'ryapman. Uning tashqi ko'rinishi juda diqqatga sazovor, kulrang sviter ustidan kiyilgan to'q sariq jilet sahnaga rang qo'shadi. Quyoshdan saqlaydigan ko'zoynaklar quyoshli kunni ko'rsatadi, bu uning tashqarida nima uchun yurganini tushuntirishi mumkin. Uning yelkasidagi ryukzak u sayohatda ekanligini yoki shunchaki muhim joyga ketayotganini ko'rsatadi. Orqa fondagi shahar manzarasi, baland binolar va gavjum ko'chalar bilan, shahar hayotining qizg'inligini aks ettiradi, "hech qachon uxlamaydigan shahar". Bu surat metropoliten hayotining mohiyatini aks ettiradi, go'yo hamma doim harakatda.

Ikkinchi suratga kelsak, unda turli yoshdagi yo'lovchilar bilan to'lgan avtobus ichki qismi tasvirlangan, ularning har biri o'z olami bilan band. Old tomondagi keksa juftlik mening e'tiborimni tortadi, ayniqsa smartfonga berilib ketgan ayol, bu texnologiya avlodlar o'rtasidagi tafovutni qanday bartaraf etishini ko'rsatadi. Avtobusning yorqin ko'k va sariq ichki qismi bu odatiy sahnaga yorqinlik qo'shadi. Uzoqroqda, yosh yo'lovchilar yoki suhbatlashib o'tirishibdi yoki o'zlarining raqamli olamiga sho'ng'ib ketishgan, bu esa jamoat transporti jamiyatning kichik bir ko'rinishiga aylanishini ko'rsatadi. Bu suratlar, shunchalik farqli bo'lishiga qaramay, insoniy aloqa va kundalik hayot haqida hikoya qilishi juda hayratlanarli.

questions.prompt: Which is more comfortable: a bus or a taxi?
questions.sampleA2:
I think taxi is better.

Because bus is crowded and noisy.

Taxi is more quiet and I like it.
questions.sampleB1:
Well, I think a taxi is probably more comfortable than a bus.

For example, in a taxi, you can usually sit down and relax.

However, buses can be very crowded, especially during rush hour.

Also, taxis are faster, so you don't have to spend as much time travelling.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'd go with a taxi any day. The thing is, you get the whole space to yourself, so you can just sit back and relax without being squashed in. A bus can get really packed at rush hour. That said, a taxi does burn a hole in your pocket, so it's a bit of a trade-off.

Xo'sh, menimcha, taksi avtobusga qaraganda ancha qulayroq.

Masalan, taksida odatda o'tirib dam olishingiz mumkin.

Biroq, avtobuslar juda gavjum bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa tirbandlik paytida.

Shuningdek, taksilar tezroq, shuning uchun sayohatga unchalik ko'p vaqt sarflashingizga to'g'ri kelmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Umuman olganda, men taksi avtobusga qaraganda qulayroq tajriba taklif qiladi deb aytgan bo'lardim, garchi bu vaziyatga bog'liq.

Avtobuslar tejamkorroq variant bo'lsa-da, qulaylik darajasi ko'pincha odamlar gavjumligi va tez-tez to'xtashlar tufayli buziladi.

Taksilar esa, aksincha, shaxsiy va to'g'ridan-to'g'ri sayohatni ta'minlaydi.

Siz haroratni nazorat qilishingiz, o'z musiqangizni tinglashingiz va odatda jamoat transportida uchraydigan bezovtaliklarsiz dam olishingiz mumkin.

Albatta, bu yuqori narxga ega, shuning uchun bu qulaylik va arzonlik o'rtasidagi murosadir.

"I'd have to say that the comfort level really depends on the circumstances of the journey." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, qulaylik darajasi haqiqatda sayohat sharoitlariga bog'liq."

questions.sampleAnswer:
When discussing comfort, I genuinely believe that taking a taxi offers a more personalized and relaxed experience compared to a bus. "Different strokes for different folks," but for me, the level of convenience and privacy a taxi provides is truly unmatched. First of all, in a taxi, you're not confined to a schedule. You can pick up a taxi at any time, which is incredibly beneficial if you're running late or need to reach a destination swiftly.

Moreover, taxis allow for a direct route to your destination, eliminating the frequent stops that characterize bus journeys. This means you can sit back and relax without having to worry about the hustle and bustle of other passengers. Last month, I had an early morning flight, and I opted for a taxi. It was remarkably comfortable as I could let my hair down and enjoy the quiet ride to the airport.

On the other hand, buses can be a mixed bag when it comes to comfort. They're significantly cheaper, which is a budget-friendly option for many. However, the experience varies depending on the time of day and location. During peak hours, buses can get crowded and noisy, making it hard to find a seat, let alone enjoy the ride.

In conclusion, while both modes of transportation have their own merits, I honestly find taxis to be a more comfortable choice for those who prioritize convenience and personal space.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Qulaylik haqida gap ketganda, men taksida yurish avtobusga nisbatan ko'proq shaxsiy va xotirjam tajriba taqdim etadi deb chin dildan ishonaman. "Har kimning o'z didi bor", lekin men uchun taksi ta'minlaydigan qulaylik va maxfiylik darajasi haqiqatan ham beqiyosdir. Birinchidan, taksida siz jadvalga bog'lanib qolmaysiz. Siz istalgan vaqtda taksi olishingiz mumkin, bu agar siz kech qolsangiz yoki biror joyga tezda yetib borishingiz kerak bo'lsa, juda foydali.

Bundan tashqari, taksilar sizning manzilingizga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yo'nalishga imkon beradi, bu esa avtobus safarlariga xos bo'lgan tez-tez to'xtashlarni yo'q qiladi. Bu shuni anglatadiki, siz boshqa yo'lovchilarning shovqini haqida qayg'urmasdan bemalol o'tirib dam olishingiz mumkin. O'tgan oyda ertalab reysim bor edi va men taksini tanladim. Men sochlarimni yoyib, aeroportga tinch sayohatdan bahra olganim uchun juda qulay edi.

Boshqa tomondan, avtobuslar qulaylik nuqtai nazaridan aralash bo'lishi mumkin. Ular ancha arzon, bu ko'pchilik uchun byudjetga mos variant. Biroq, tajriba kunning vaqtiga va joyiga qarab o'zgaradi. Eng gavjum paytlarda avtobuslar olomon va shovqinli bo'lib ketishi mumkin, bu esa o'tirishga, hatto sayohatdan zavqlanishga ham xalaqit beradi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, transportning ikkala turining ham o'z afzalliklari bor bo'lsa-da, men shaxsan qulaylik va shaxsiy makonga ustunlik beradiganlar uchun taksilar qulayroq tanlov deb bilaman.

"Every little helps", and when it comes to the environment, this "rings especially true". I genuinely believe that people should opt for public transport like buses over taxis whenever feasible. Firstly, using buses is incredibly beneficial from a sustainability perspective. Buses can carry a large number of passengers simultaneously, which significantly reduces the carbon footprint per person compared to taxis. Furthermore, public transport systems are constantly being improved to be more efficient and convenient, making them a viable alternative to private hire vehicles.

Moreover, the economic aspect cannot be overlooked. Public transportation is substantially more cost-effective, which can be particularly advantageous for people who live on a shoestring budget. I remember when I was a student, I would rely heavily on buses to get around the city. It saved me a pretty penny over the years, allowing me to allocate funds to other necessities.

That being said, I acknowledge that taxis do have their place, particularly for direct routes and when time is of the essence. However, if we are to consider the bigger picture, promoting the use of buses as a primary mode of transport could lead to tangible benefits for society as a whole. "The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step", and choosing to use public transport more regularly is one such step towards a sustainable future.

questions.sampleB2: Right, so an achievement I'm genuinely proud of is running my first half-marathon last year. To be honest, I'd never been much of a runner, so signing up felt like a massive leap of faith. I trained for months, dragging myself out of bed at the crack of dawn, and there were plenty of times I wanted to throw in the towel. As for how success varies, I suppose it really is in the eye of the beholder. For me personally, success isn't about ticking boxes or keeping up with everyone else. It's about growing as a person and staying true to what matters to me. At the end of the day, one person's dream might mean nothing to somebody else, and I think that's what makes the whole idea of success so fascinating.

bulletPoints: Describe an achievement that you consider a personal success.
How did this success influence your approach to future goals?
How does the definition of success vary between cultures or individuals?
questions.sampleAnswer:
One of the most significant achievements that I consider a personal success was when I managed to set up my own online business. At the outset, I faced numerous challenges, but I was determined to see it through. This venture was born out of a "necessity is the mother of invention" situation, as I found myself eager to explore entrepreneurial avenues. After months of meticulous planning and market research, the business began to thrive.

This success profoundly influenced my approach to future goals, as it taught me the importance of resilience and adaptability. I realized that it's crucial to stay on top of industry trends and be open to feedback. As a result, I have become more strategic in my planning, often breaking down larger goals into manageable milestones, which has been incredibly effective in achieving them.

The definition of success can vary greatly between cultures or individuals. For some, success might mean having a stable family life; for others, it could be climbing the corporate ladder. For instance, in many Western societies, individual achievements and material wealth are often seen as benchmarks of success. In contrast, in more collectivist cultures, success might be measured by the ability to contribute to the community or family. Personally, I believe success is intrinsically linked to personal satisfaction and the ability to find one's niche in this world.

Men shaxsiy muvaffaqiyat deb hisoblaydigan eng muhim yutuqlardan biri bu o'z onlayn biznesimni yo'lga qo'yganim bo'ldi. Boshida men ko'plab qiyinchiliklarga duch keldim, lekin men uni oxirigacha yetkazishga qat'iy qaror qilgan edim. Bu tadbirkorlik yo'llarini o'rganishga intilganim sababli, bu tashabbus "ehtiyoj ixtironing onasi" vaziyatidan kelib chiqqan edi. Bir necha oylik puxta rejalashtirish va bozor tadqiqotlaridan so'ng, biznes rivojlana boshladi.

Bu muvaffaqiyat kelajakdagi maqsadlarimga bo'lgan yondashuvimga chuqur ta'sir ko'rsatdi, chunki u menga chidamlilik va moslashuvchanlikning muhimligini o'rgatdi. Men sanoat tendentsiyalaridan xabardor bo'lish va fikr-mulohazalarga ochiq bo'lish muhimligini angladim. Natijada, men rejalashtirishda yanada strategik bo'lib qoldim, ko'pincha katta maqsadlarni boshqariladigan bosqichlarga bo'lib chiqaman, bu ularga erishishda juda samarali bo'ldi.

Muvaffaqiyatning ta'rifi madaniyatlar yoki shaxslar o'rtasida juda katta farq qilishi mumkin. Kimdir uchun muvaffaqiyat barqaror oilaviy hayotga ega bo'lishni anglatishi mumkin; boshqalar uchun bu korporativ zinapoyadan ko'tarilish bo'lishi mumkin. Misol uchun, ko'plab G'arb jamiyatlarida individual yutuqlar va moddiy boylik ko'pincha muvaffaqiyat mezonlari sifatida qaraladi. Aksincha, ko'proq kollektivistik madaniyatlarda muvaffaqiyat jamiyatga yoki oilaga hissa qo'shish qobiliyati bilan o'lchanishi mumkin. Shaxsan men, muvaffaqiyat shaxsiy qoniqish va bu dunyoda o'z o'rnini topish qobiliyati bilan chambarchas bog'liq deb hisoblayman.

questions.sampleA2:
I think animal testing is bad.

questions.sampleB1:
I think animal testing is a difficult issue.

questions.sampleB2: Well, this is a really tricky one, and I can honestly see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, there's a strong case for banning it. Animal testing can be incredibly cruel, and many people feel it's just morally wrong to make animals suffer for our sake. For a lot of people, it's a genuine ethical dilemma. On top of that, alternatives like advanced computer modelling and lab-grown tissue are coming on leaps and bounds, so you could argue we don't need to rely on animals as much as we used to. That said, I do think the other side has a point too. The thing is, a lot of life-saving medicines and treatments simply wouldn't exist without animal testing. Supporters would say that strict regulations are in place to make sure it's carried out as humanely as possible, and that for certain diseases, testing on animals is still the only reliable way to check a new drug is safe before it reaches people. Weighing it all up, I can see why a worldwide ban sounds appealing in principle, but I'm not sure banning it overnight is realistic just yet. If I had to pin my colours to the mast, I'd say the sensible way forward is to keep pouring money into alternatives and phase animal testing out gradually, rather than pulling the plug all at once. At the end of the day, it's about striking a balance between protecting animal welfare and keeping people safe, and honestly, that's easier said than done.

questions.sampleAnswer: "The greatness of a nation can be judged by the way its animals are treated." This poignant quote by Mahatma Gandhi serves as a powerful reminder of our ethical obligations towards animals. The topic of animal testing is undoubtedly a contentious issue, with valid arguments on both sides. Firstly, there is compelling evidence to suggest that animal testing is incredibly cruel and inhumane. Animals in laboratories often endure significant suffering, leading many to argue that it is our moral duty to phase out such practices. Furthermore, the advancement of technology has brought about innovative alternatives like computer models and in vitro testing. These methods are rapidly advancing and have shown promise in replicating human biology without the ethical implications of animal testing. Moreover, it is entirely possible to conduct medical research without harming animals. Many researchers have pioneered alternative techniques that produce reliable results, offering hope for a future where animal testing is done away with completely. On the other hand, there are those who vehemently argue that animal testing is essential for the development of life-saving medicines and treatments. It is asserted that some diseases are too complex to be studied through alternatives alone, thus necessitating animal testing to ensure the safety of new drugs for humans. Additionally, strict regulations have been put in place to ensure that animal testing is conducted humanely and responsibly, minimizing the suffering of animals to the greatest extent possible. However, while these regulations are crucial, they cannot make up for the fundamental ethical concerns that many people have regarding animal testing. In my opinion, while animal testing has undoubtedly contributed to medical advancements, it is high time we move towards more ethical and humane alternatives. The ongoing progress in technology offers us the chance to step into a new era of research that respects the sanctity of all living beings. Rome wasn't built in a day, but by prioritizing innovation and ethics, we can aspire to a future where animal testing is no longer seen as a necessary evil.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
"Bir millatning buyukligi uning hayvonlarga bo'lgan munosabati bilan baholanadi." Mahatma Gandining ushbu ta'sirchan iqtidasi bizning hayvonlarga nisbatan axloqiy majburiyatlarimizni kuchli eslatma bo'lib xizmat qiladi. Hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish mavzusi, shubhasiz, bahsli masala bo'lib, har ikki tomonda ham asosli dalillar mavjud.

Birinchidan, hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish nihoyatda shafqatsiz va insoniylikka zid ekanligini ko'rsatadigan ishonchli dalillar mavjud. Laboratoriyalardagi hayvonlar ko'pincha sezilarli azob chekishadi, bu esa ko'pchilikni bunday amaliyotlarni bosqichma-bosqich bekor qilish bizning axloqiy burchimizdir, deb ta'kidlashga undaydi. Bundan tashqari, texnologiyaning rivojlanishi kompyuter modellari va in vitro sinovlari kabi innovatsion alternativlarni keltirib chiqardi. Ushbu usullar tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanmoqda va hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazishning axloqiy oqibatlarisiz inson biologiyasini takrorlashda umid baxsh etdi.

Bundan tashqari, hayvonlarga zarar bermasdan tibbiy tadqiqotlar o'tkazish butunlay mumkin. Ko'pgina tadqiqotchilar ishonchli natijalar beradigan muqobil usullarni ishlab chiqdilar va hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish butunlay bekor qilinadigan kelajakka umid uyg'otdilar.

Boshqa tomondan, hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish hayotni saqlab qoluvchi dori-darmonlar va davolash usullarini ishlab chiqish uchun zarur, deb qat'iy turib oladiganlar ham bor. Ba'zi kasalliklar faqatgina muqobil usullar orqali o'rganish uchun juda murakkab ekanligi, shuning uchun odamlar uchun yangi dorilarning xavfsizligini ta'minlash uchun hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish zarurligi ta'kidlanadi.

Bundan tashqari, hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish insoniylik bilan va mas'uliyat bilan amalga oshirilishini ta'minlash uchun qat'iy qoidalar joriy etilgan bo'lib, hayvonlarning azoblanishini imkon qadar kamaytirishga qaratilgan. Biroq, ushbu qoidalar muhim bo'lsa-da, ular ko'pchilik odamlarda hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish bilan bog'liq bo'lgan asosiy axloqiy xavotirlarni qoplay olmaydi.
